correctness.rationale: Every candidate 8-edge subset of the 12-edge nine-vertex grid is tested (495 total), and every signed character is evaluated (4096 total). Independent exact methods, the tree incidence Walsh butterfly and the 8-by-8 signed-Laplacian Bareiss determinants, reproduce the 15-level histogram. Edge counts 136 (perimeter) and 112 (interior) yield 4-divisibility; frequency mask 116 attains 4, zero mask 47 witnesses cancellation. The Fourier support indicator gives inverse-Walsh absolute numerator sum 40976, so the endpoint projection norm is 2561/256. Translation averaging proves optimality among all projections onto the range. Both embedded checkers were executed successfully, with no floating-point approximations.

value.rationale: The nine-vertex free-boundary square grid is the first square grid with a genuine interior vertex, beyond all two-rail ladders. The exact 1186-dimensional Fourier blind space, nonzero spectral gap 4, and optimal endpoint projection norm 2561/256 jointly quantify recoverability, Hilbert deconvolution stability, and worst-case endpoint amplification. The precisely defined natural grid has a finite but complete spectral classification that can be used as a benchmark for any extension to higher grid widths. These are not automatic consequences of its classical 192 spanning-tree count.
